GET /v1/keys.description: List your issuer signing keys and the JWKS (JSON Web Key Set) discovery URI. You use this endpoint to inspect active and rotated keys before or after a rotation. The service creates an active signing key on first use when none exists.

200.description: You receive the tenant's signing keys and the JWKS (JSON Web Key Set) URI that verifiers use to discover public keys.

keys.description: Signing keys the tenant still publishes for verification. The list includes active and rotated keys, ordered newest first.

id.description: Internal UUID of the signing-key record.

kid.description: JWK (JSON Web Key) key identifier for the public signing key. The service places this `kid` in each SD-JWT VC (Selective-Disclosure JWT Verifiable Credential) header so verifiers can select the right public key.

alg.description: JSON Web Signature algorithm used by this key.

status.description: Key lifecycle state. `active` signs new credentials. `rotated` verifies credentials signed before rotation.

is_active.description: Whether this key is the current signing key.

valid_until.description: Timestamp until which a rotated key remains valid for verification. Active keys return null.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the signing key was created.

jwks_uri.description: Absolute JWKS (JSON Web Key Set) discovery URL for this tenant. The document exposes public JWK (JSON Web Key) values for active and rotated keys.

POST /v1/keys/rotate.description: Rotate your issuer signing key. You can send `overlap_days` to choose how long credentials signed by the previous key keep verifying. New credentials use the new active key immediately.

overlap_days.description: Number of days the previous key remains valid after rotation. Use this to control the overlap window for credentials already signed by that key.

201.description: The rotation result, including the new key, the rotated key, the requested overlap window, and the impact summary.

new_key.description: The new signing key. The service uses this key to sign credentials after rotation.

id.description: Internal UUID of the new signing-key record.

kid.description: JWK (JSON Web Key) key identifier for the new active key. Credentials issued after rotation carry this `kid` in their SD-JWT VC (Selective-Disclosure JWT Verifiable Credential) header.

alg.description: JSON Web Signature algorithm used by the new key.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the new key after rotation.

is_active.description: Whether this key is the current signing key.

valid_until.description: Validity expiry for the key. The active key returns null.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the new key was created.

rotated_key.description: The previous active signing key after the service demotes it to `rotated`. Credentials already signed by this key keep verifying until `valid_until`.

id.description: Internal UUID of the rotated signing-key record.

kid.description: JWK (JSON Web Key) key identifier for the rotated key. Credentials signed before rotation carry this `kid` in their SD-JWT VC (Selective-Disclosure JWT Verifiable Credential) header.

alg.description: JSON Web Signature algorithm used by the rotated key.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the previous active key after rotation.

is_active.description: Whether this key is the current signing key.

valid_until.description: Timestamp until which the rotated key remains valid for verification.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the rotated key was created.

overlap_days.description: Number of days the rotated key remains valid for credentials signed before rotation.

impact.description: Summary of how the rotation affects credentials already signed by the previous key.

credentials_under_previous_key.description: Count of credentials signed by the previous key when you rotated it.

note.description: Human-readable explanation of the overlap window after rotation.
note.example: Existing credentials keep verifying under the rotated key for 7 days (overlapping validity); new credentials sign with the new key immediately.

GET /v1/keys/impact.description: Preview how many issued credentials use the active key before you rotate it. You use this endpoint to decide whether the default overlap window is acceptable.

200.description: The rotation-impact preview for the tenant.

credentials_under_active_key.description: Count of credentials signed by the active key before rotation.

default_overlap_days.description: Default number of days the service keeps the rotated key trusted when you do not provide `overlap_days`.

note.description: Human-readable explanation of the overlap behavior.
note.example: These credentials would continue to verify under the current key after rotation (overlapping validity).

GET /v1/status-lists/{slug}/{uuid}.description: Public, unauthenticated fetch of an entire IETF Token Status List compressed bitstring used for SD-JWT VC (Selective-Disclosure JWT Verifiable Credential) revocation and suspension. Verifiers fetch the whole list and read the bit at a credential's status index. Serving the full list instead of a single entry helps defend against correlation.

params.name: slug
params.description: The issuer tenant's URL slug. It scopes the lookup to that tenant.

params.name: uuid
params.description: UUID of the status list to fetch. It must belong to the tenant identified by `slug`.

200.description: The full status list as a base64url-encoded bitstring plus its URI and size.

uri.description: Canonical absolute URI of this status list. Credentials reference this value from their status claim.

size.description: Number of bits in the status list.

bits_b64.description: Status-list bitstring encoded as a base64url string. Decode it and read the bit at a credential's status index.
